title: Change Conversations software and contracts
summary: Modify the Conversations library, CLI, App Server compatibility, normalization, packaging, tests, or documentation.
use_when: Conversations code, tests, protocol behavior, public schema, Chancery contract, packaging, release workflow, or documentation is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is ordinary use of the installed Conversations CLI.
Release publication or installed deployment has not been separately authorized.
outcome: A minimal tested Conversations change that preserves the App Server-only storage boundary and whose public and operational contracts match the implementation.
effects: Modifies Conversations source, tests, documentation, packaging, or authored contracts.
A public-schema or compatibility change can affect local consumers of the Conversations Rust library and JSON output.
Release and deployment remain separate effects.
authority: Conversations owns its typed normalized schema, CLI, filters, deduplication, and packaging.
Codex App Server remains the sole authority for conversation discovery and storage compatibility.
No implementation shortcut may create raw JSONL or SQLite coupling.
success: The smallest owning code and exact documents agree.
Fake App Server tests cover every affected protocol and normalization boundary.
Process-lifecycle tests prove descendant cleanup remains scoped to the private launch group when that boundary changes.
failure_and_recovery: Do not turn incomplete App Server data into a successful partial corpus.
Preserve the legacy fallback only for unavailable turn pagination, not arbitrary read errors.
Packaging changes retain content identity, tamper detection, prior selectors, and post-switch rollback.
privacy: Fixtures must be synthetic; release bundles must never contain real transcript data.
Diagnostics and JSON examples should avoid private paths and conversation text.
steps: Read `AGENTS.md` and the exact architecture, CLI, installation, and Chancery documents for the changed behavior.
Consult the current official Codex App Server documentation before changing protocol assumptions.
Implement the smallest change with synthetic App Server fixtures and update shared contracts in the same change.
Run `./ci.sh`; run release or deployment only under separate authorization.
checkpoints: No code reads Codex JSONL or SQLite files.
Default output remains user/assistant-only, root-task-only, active-and-archived, and state-database-only.
Turn and thread pagination, copied-item deduplication, and incomplete-read failure remain proved.
CI passes without publishing or deploying.
adaptation: Regenerate or consult the version-matched App Server schema when a documented method or field differs across installed Codex versions.
Scale fake-server coverage to the changed boundary without adding a raw-storage fallback.
stop_when: The desired data is unavailable through the documented App Server API.
A public-schema change would silently break an existing local library consumer.
The change would require task mutation, a persistent index, or raw Codex storage access outside the approved product boundary.
does_not_authorize: Running `release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Mutating Codex tasks or accessing private Codex storage directly.
